title: Offboarding a Delegate strands their delegators' voting power instead of returning it
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.5.4 states the consequence of any offboarding: "the Delegate's status in the Registry of Delegates is updated to Inactive. SPK delegators must **manually** revoke their delegations and redelegate if they wish to continue participating in Spark governance."

Nothing reverts automatically. The delegation remains pointed at a delegate who is no longer permitted to vote, so the delegated power neither votes nor returns to its owner. It simply stops counting.

The failure mode is quiet and asymmetric. Delegates are removed by mechanisms that require no delegator involvement and, in the non-performance and term-end cases, no announcement a holder would necessarily see: automatic offboarding for missed votes (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.5.2), immediate Risk Council removal (.5.3), and 00:00 UTC term-end lapse (.5.5). A holder who delegated once and stopped paying attention loses their voice without ever being told, and the framework's only mitigation is that the Operational Facilitator posts a Sky Forum notice.

This interacts badly with the term-expiry-by-default rule. Every six months an entire cohort can lapse at once, potentially stranding a large share of delegated supply simultaneously — which lowers the absolute number of votes needed to pass a proposal and quietly concentrates influence among the attentive. Non-participation caused by administrative expiry is indistinguishable, at the tally, from deliberate abstention.
description: Registry status flips to Inactive but delegations persist; delegators must manually revoke and redelegate, so an inattentive holder is silently disenfranchised.
